this is inarguably one of the best games I have ever played. You can feel the passion from the team that worked on it throughout every single scene, line of dialogue, every journal entry. This game can change your perception of the world if you let it. It's beautiful and I couldnt recommend any game more than this one.

I absolutely loved this game. I fell in love with the friendships and overall relationships you make during the story, and the general art style and humor made it all feel extremely cozy. Made me feel a lot of things as I could relate very deeply with Mae, things that took me a long time to identify.

Lots of hard hitting quotes as well.... also, EEEEEELS MOM

It's actually super boring! You just live in a small town as a cat, talk to people, do daily stuff.

If real life simulators is your thing, then this game will be good for you. But if you like adventures, then this game will be very boring!
Emotional and gentle, if you're looking for a game to get invested in, this is it folks

Strong narrative
Great plot
Lovable characters with distinct personalities
Marvellous World-building
And a brilliant soundtrack

In my opinion 10/10

Alec, Scott and the team have made something special with this one, the project oozes with passion, I look forward to see where the team goes in the future.

Definitely worth checking out, It would be a real shame not to experience it for yourself.

RIP A.H

If you had to choose only one story based game to play then Night in the Woods wins by a landslide.

It has fantastic atmosphere, an amazing soundtrack, a great art style, lovable characters, and everything in between.

Buy. This. Game.

Some games should really be graphic novels, and this game is no exception. The platforming, rhythm playing and dungeon crawling is all pretty basic, and doesn't add anything new.

However, the story in this game is really remarkable. It starts slow, but once you get into the rhythm, the game has a charm that is really quaint as you go through your days trying to make sense of things as a college dropout, who returns to her hometown. What unfolds as you play is story that touches on family, friends, community, home, God, abuse, love, life, death, loss, faith, despair and hope.

Some of my favorite sentiments are reinforced in this game. The idea of making and finding meaning in the people around us, in a cruel, often unfeeling world is always beautiful. This is a game with something to say, and it says it well. I can't recommend it enough.

"Nothing is gonna save us forever, but a lot of things can save us today."

A very colorful and wonderful game about friendship and exploring. This shows how the smallest things you do can have an effect on others, from giving them the courage to put themselves out there or bringing people together. Talk to everyone you can to get the most out of it.

I thought I did everything on the first run but missed some stuff. I focused on what I missed and skipped over what I had done already, some of the changes in people were noticable all because I did not interact with them. Did give me some thoughts to ponder.

There are some touchy subjects but the music and art style are really calming and simple.

Also crimes, do lots of crimes.

High concept themes, music, dialogue, and character studies. Annoying quick time and repetitive game play. Typical of this genre. Still weird that a 2D game with talking animals has better character interaction/ dialogue than most AAA games.

I absolutely love this game! Night in the Woods just has this feel about it, a cozy, spooky, heartfelt, adventurous feel. Its a story that sucks you in and gets you invested. You just want to keep exploring, find that next hidden thing, get to the top of that building, play the songs over and over! Feed. Those. Rats! Night in the woods get a solid 13/10 rating from me!! <3

Incredible game, can be very depressing at times. Hard to play through just because the content brings up a lot of different things. But overall worth it. I highly enjoyed meeting greg and the crocodile shawty all the time.
This is just the right amount of heavy vs. cute, it's so playable and fun to explore and get new achievements. Dialogue is spot on. Just so much fun!
This is genuinely probably my favorite story-driven game ever. The visuals, the mysteries, the way everything progresses, play this game and I promise you will NOT regret it one bit

This one is made of cute visuals, fierce poetry of it all, autumnal essence, familiar austerity and absolutely unforgettable music. 💔
It doesn't offer much gameplay-wise (oh, those pitiful jumps...), and overall is more like interactive comics. But very engaging, stylish and music-driven comics!
If you can read and bear the slow pace, this remarkable 🍁 treasure of a game surely won't leave you untouched (but beware of sadness triggers, though).

✨11 sinkholes out of 10!

I was really sceptical at first.

I knew what this was going to be yet didn't quite know what the game was actually about. I know that might sound strange and it kinda is, but I'm glad I got passed my fear of the minor things I had known would break me(emotionally) in this game and actually played it.

The story, characters, setting, mystery, drama, action, mini-games, interactions, knowledge and so much more are worth more than most Triple A titles nowadays in my opinion and deserves every ounce of respect it got from critics. I laughed, I cried, I was shocked and I was scared. All throughout this entire, long journey that wasn't actually all that long.

The game made me care what was going to happen, made me hate myself each time I chose something that panned out like I didn't want to, made me weigh my options heavily and in the end, made me simply feel good about the choices I had made correctly in my own opinion.

It has some replayability due to the branching path, so you'll be able to catch things you didn's the next time around.

My personal tip. Check out the entire town each day before continuing with one of the other main characters. Each side character has a story to tell, many objects do as well.

Visceral evocations of life growing up in my hometown? Check.
Advocacy for the abolition of capitalism? Check.
Thoughtful material to make sure I consider how I'm allocating my limited time with my loved ones? You betcha.

I'm only a few hours in, just going into Part 2 (don't know how many there are), and so far I'm absolutely adoring the game.

Honestly I have re-played this game so many times (mostly on my switch) & I never get bored with it.
NITW has such a good story. I would highly recommend this game to anyone wanting a slow-paced story rich game.

A game with lots of charm, a beautiful artstyle and lots of detail.
The story takes quite a bit to get rolling and it shows when being replayed.
I can still recommend playing, and replaying it to get different dialouges and exploring the world a bit.
I'm mostly very fond of this game <3

This is a beautiful entertaining game that literally crushed my heart, put it together, crushed it, pieced it together, then slam dunked it into a basket. I love this game for the story, the dialogue, the art, just everything about this makes me euphoric,

This is my favorite game of all time and I replay it all the time, It's so so so so so so good. The queer representation helped me a lot as a kid and I really appreciate it. It's always been a game I loved because of the art style, the aesthetic, and the characters and story. I will never forget NITW and I love it more than I can describe. Please play this game if you haven't and then replay it a few times to get every route. I still never get bored of it and its lovely bpbpbpbp text sounds. So wonderful. I adore it. I just wish I could reach that darned cat on the roof by Lori. I don't know what happens when you do get there, but it's always been out of my reach.

This game is a nice young adult tale. It gives me these vibes: chill, small pain & a bit sadness, loathness. But it's also real sweet. Most characters seem to be very understanding of Mae's mental state. It's nice, I wish this is how people interacted in real life. They're very thoughtful and a bit poetic.

When I feel lowest I always come back to this game. The calming music, art style, and characters are all very comforting. I relate to Mae's mental struggles and woe's heavily which plays a main part into why I enjoy it so much. Otherwise, the game is just great in general. I keep coming back to earn achievements, find things I missed, play the mini games, and just enjoy the other character's dialogue again! My only complaint would be that the first half can feel slow, and there can be cringey moments lol. I love this game to pieces, it truly is a great experience. In conclusion, I feel like everyone should watch or play through it at least once.

Night in the Woods was always a game i would come back to, its characters are incredibly down to earth and you can always relate to atleast one aspect of them all. Theyre all so incredibly lovable in their own ways, it would always hit different whenever i would play. took me several years to complete this game as i would play it for about 3 hours then not revisit it for several months at a time, it was always reliable for a nice single player experience, as i usually am not a big fan of single player games, it was different, it stood out. I found the plot interesting but yet also the times when you just hung out with the other characters and did dumb, immature things. The adventure is moving and i adore everything about it. This will be added to my very small collection of completed games.
Absolutely fantastic. Beautiful, compelling story. Incredibly deep and complex characters that really make the world feel truly alive.

One of the funnest story games I have ever played, the character development is insane it feels like a movie. I originally got this game because an old friend recommended it to me, and it is so. much. fun. The art style and the way the characters interact is definitely something I haven't come across before. I didn't know how much fun these story games could be, because before this, I would only play fps's and action adventure games. I would have never thought this game would be for me. I guess what I'm trying to say is that this game is for everyone and if you think you won't enjoy it, at least give it a try because you won't regret it.

Edit: I forgot how insane the soundtrack is, I literally bought the soundtrack after completing the game just because it was so good.

Night in the woods is a phenomenal game. it's impossible not to get attached to the characters. the story is captivating, the sequences fun, and so many positive things that I just cant list without this turning into a novel. As of recent this game has been my comfort game per se, i've been kinda using it to clear my mind off of some things and i've been playing it while I wait for my new health insurance cards. the wait is long, but it's helping me through the long run until then.

also, gregg is best boy, I want to kiss him and hug him.
This is hands down my favorite game of all time. No competition. if you're into these types of games, i highly recommend. This game no joke changed my life

Story is a little slow at first but it gets better the more you play. Loved the characters and the humor the game has. You can play this game for quite some hours if you take the time to look at the whole town every day and talk to the different characters every time you get the chance, which I would recommend doing because you might miss out on some cool things otherwise. Thumbs up :)

At this point, I am sure that this game has reached most of the audience that would be interested in a game like this (think, Undertale fans), so I'm going to pitch this to anyone that normally is not interested in this type of experiences but got their attention caught well enough to find themselves reading this review. So, here it comes:
If you're a millennial (specially a late millennial) or a zoomer, you have to play this game. There's no way you won't relate with all characters in one way or another, and there's no way you won't en up emotionally invested with every single one of them. Even if you're normally not into story-focused or dialog-heavy games, or at all, let this be an exception. And is not like there aren't fun things to do within the game, there are several minigames, exploration and an element of mystery that keep things interesting through out your play through.

It's also runs natively on Linux, so you can play it the newly released Steam Deck no problems!
Beautiful game. Great Characters. AMAZING soundtrack and storyline. Can't really go wrong. Great game to chill out and play with. Would recommend to everyone.

Existential Crisis: The Game

I didn't want to relive the year I dropped out of University, but this game did it in such a beautiful way.
Visually stunning, the music and sound design is incredible, characters have well defined personalities, everything is just charming.

But it's the story that really makes this game. The writing is just so authentic, it's like you are inside the world of a really good book. You make a lot of choices too regarding dialogue as well as relationships you have.

I've never related to a video game on such a personal level as I did with this one. The universe doesn't care about you, but that doesn't mean you stop caring about things that matter to you. I just wish I'd played this years ago so it could have helped me learn that sooner.

I played this game when I was super depressed and really going through it. As a young adult and certified dropout, this game just kept giving kick after kick straight to my teeth. It was awesome. I truly don't think I've experienced a story in any medium that made me feel so seen and observed as this game.

The gameplay itself is average, and getting from destination to destination can be somewhat tedious, but your exploration is rewarded if you do enough random walking about town. Multiple times I was pleasantly surprised when I stumbled into a different corner of Possum Springs with some story going on that I could've completely missed if I was just beelining it straight to Gregg or Bea. It helps Possum Springs feel alive.

The story is definitely where this game shines, though. If you like games with, frankly, pretty minimum game mechanics, and a story that wants to punch you in the gut to remind you just how human it is despite all the animal-shaped characters on screen, play this game. It was a delight to play and I didn't even get to touch on the atmosphere and art direction. This game is everything.

Playing this game during fall and as a 20-year-old college sophomore really hits close to home...I also wanted to learn how to play bass for a long time too (she's literally me!!)
Seeing Mae go on random side quests with different folks in town was really fun and the scene with her mom was so touching...I miss my mom TT

Finally got around to playing this game and wow. Absolutely loved it. I've never felt so seen by and enamored with a video game world, especially one so clearly based on our own. Night in the Woods is really really special and feels so relevant, even 7 years after its release. One of my favorite games now, can't recommend it enough 
--∅--
An absolute joy to play. Was just as good now as it was when I played it 7 years ago. Introspective and deep, with a thrilling mystery to unfold. Just a fantastic game.

I feel like I shouldn't even be writing this review because I'm still processing everything. Is this game worth it? Yes. Yes. It is worth twice to three times what I paid for it. Profound, beautifully animated, great characters, great music, runs smoothly, everything you could want and more. Also, as a depressed person, also deeply cathartic to see some things put to words like this.

It was a constant surprise. Story is reaaaaally well thought out, characters are really well made. It is not a "psychological horror", but might consider it "horror" by design.

I do not appreciate all achievements being hidden, that's non-sense. Most achievements shouldn't be hidden. If it is the spoilers the concern, then use locked achievements' descriptions/names as hints!

I also love how so many characters are obviously queer. It's so refreshing, and the game so good.

so uh - i have a fEW mental illnesses and have been through some rough times. i have made some horrible mistakes and made many lives (my own included) hell.

this game speaks to me on a level i don't know how to describe. when i am the most numb and in deepest anhedonia, this game helps. reminds me what it feels like when people care, when people are worried. what it feels like to matter even when you can't convince yourself that you do.

this is easily one of my favorite games and i will replay it at least once a year for the forseeable future.

You probably gonna love it if you're 19-24 y.o. and mildly (or more) depressed.
Great game. Funny, spooky, kinda philosophical and utterly relatable.

P.S. thx for gifting it to me, Stas. Became a college dropout soon after.

This is the best game I've ever played. 10/10 story, 10/10 art, 10/10 character development, 10/10 everything. I've never related or connected to characters as much as in this game. 

GREGG RULZ OK

genuinely nothing else like it. i loved mae and her friends. i loved exploring the town and talking to everyone. learning about possum springs. hanging out with friends. discovering scenes i’ve never seen before when watching playthroughs.

i discovered NITW years ago and find myself returning to it over and over again. 11/10 i wish i could discover it for the first time all over again.

I haven't been feeling the best. I'm at a major turning point in my life and things have been rough. I've doubted myself, my ability, my friends, and everything around me.

Playing this game helped me feel not alone. And by the end of it, I wanted to live more than ever.

It's just shapes but these shapes mean something to me. Something very important.

Rest in peace, Alec Holowka.

highly recommending this game to people who are done with college or their education in general. The atmosphere is gorgeous, the characters are likable and relatable. The game puts you into familiar settings that most of us has to face one time or another. Topics about anxiety, growing up, losing or regaining connections with people, letting go of the past and much more.
I really wanna add more, but right now if you haven't tried this game yet, I am not going to sit here and spoil everything. This is an experience type of game and I want you to have a blast figuring out all of the small things that night in the woods can offer you.

I have to admit...
When I first saw this game on kickstarter couple of years ago I did not think it would be this great.
The story, the characters, the artstyle and the atmosphere - every single thing in this game is made with so much effort and care, and in the end we have a legitimately fun, deep game. Well done, guys, well done.

Gregg rulez ok

This game is legit S tier back when it first came out I watched videos and fell in love with the game but after playing it for the first time ever the videos don't do it justice you need to play it yourself to experience how good it really is
Relatable characters and interactions. Plenty of humor to balance issues centered around mental health. Wonderful game with a great art style.
Peaceful, haunting, beautiful music, interesting decision-making, fun minigames, charming characters. There's everything to love and nothing to dislike. Highly recommend multiple playthroughs.

Very beautiful and quirky. If you don't like Mae as a character and is annoyed by her from the start then the game probably isn't worth it, but if your like me and mentally ill then it's a solid 9/10 experience.

Its really good game for 2 playthroughts after that you will start doing the same stuff again.
Awesome soundtrack writing and graphics through I have stutter only in this game on high end pc

This has become one of my favourite games omg, Idk if i can put into words just how much I loved everything about this, from the artstyle to the gameplay, and the dialogue. I heavily recommend, absolute cinema!!
